newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurostocks gain, Ldn slips from early record.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurostocks gain, Ldn slips from early record.

text.p: Some European bourses made steep gains on Thursday, encouraged by Wall Street's record overnight close, but London slipped from an early trading peak because of uncertainty over the direction of interest rates.

In currencies, the dollar remained near eight-year highs against the mark but the British pound drifted lower with investors jittery over whether the Bank of England would increase rates for the fourth month in a row.

London's volatile performance was a main focus of attention. After storming to a record close on Wednesday, past a 5,000-point milestone on the FTSE index, stocks opened at a new intra-day high, only to tumble into the minus column by mid-morning.

The engine driving London's bull run is a weakening of the pound from recent peaks, which is seen improving profits for exporters. But worries over an increase in interest rates, which would boost sterling, have the opposite effect.

"It all feels a bit unreal, with people seeing the magic 5,000 level and getting sucked in with dollar signs in their eyes," said a dealer as the FTSE slipped from an all-time high of 5,048.4 points to 5,017.5. It closed on Wednesday at 5,026.2.
"You can seen how vulnerable the market is. Everyone's scared of being caught short and at the same time as soon as you see any selling pressure, prices come off very sharpish," said another dealer.
Investors were awaiting the outcome of a two-day meeting of Bank of England policy-makers later on Thursday.

Many believe that rates would be increased further to contain inflationary pressures, while others say the Bank would not sanction another rise because of complaints from exporters badly hit by the pound's strength.

"If rates go up a quarter point, it will not do a huge amount of damage to equities," said Charterhouse group chief economist Richard Jeffrey. "If they go up half a point, it would make investors sit up and think."
Britain's Confederation of British Industry (CBI) warned that a rate rise could turn economic slowdown into a grinding halt.
"I don't think that we ought to see interest rates go up again today," said CBI chief economist Kate Barker in a BBC Radio interview.

In Frankfurt, stocks soared by more than 1.5 percent, lifted by Wall Street's record close at 8,259.51 points on the Dow Jones Industrial Average, up 71.77. The dollar's advance towards 1.89 marks also helped underpin the market.
Dealers said the German share market had a positive undertone and looked for further gains during the session despite modest losses in the German debt market.
The market focus remained on banking shares with Deutsche Bank among the top volume shares, rising 1.35 marks to 119 marks, amid speculation about further banking industry mergers or takeovers.
Commerzbank, considered a top takeover target, was up 23 pfennigs at 62.70, while Dresdner Bank was up 89 pfennigs at 79.50 marks.

The Paris bourse also opened more than one percent higher, bolstered by Wall Street and receding interest rate worries. Stocks eased back slightly by mid-morning but still showed gains of 0.6 percent.
In currency markets, the dollar climbed half a pfennig to 1.8809 marks, near its highest levels against the German currency since October 1989.
Concern about the potential for trade tensions between the United States and Japan was kept alive by remarks made on Wednesday by U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky.

Despite these worries, the dollar held on to most of its gains to 12-week highs against the Japanese currency on Wednesday. By mid-morning it was at 118.70 yen, compared to 118.61 in late trade the previous day.
Sterling was vulnerable after a sell-off on Wednesday as expectations rose that the Bank of England might not raise interest rates.
Robert Hayward, economic adviser at Bank of America, said he expected the Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee to raise interest rates by 25 basis points to 7.00 percent.
"If that happens, we may be looking at a small-scale recovery, perhaps up to 3.04 marks," he said.
The pound was hanging on just above three marks and at $1.5935 against Wednesday's European closing levels of 3.0130 and $1.6038.
"... if they hold rates as they are, I'd expect only a modest sell-off. People would be looking for another move in September," Hayward said.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8809 marks and 118.70 yen, compared to 1.8748 and 118.61 in late trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 8.7 points at 5,017.5.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was up 67.38 points at 4,402.77 in bourse trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 16.25 points at 3,053.34.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $318.95 an ounce, compared to $319.85 at the close on Wednesday. Silver was two cents lower at $4.35.
